Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambition was to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.” There had, therefore, been widespread hope across the women’s game that 2027’s prize pot would match the men’s on at least a per-team basis. quietus.title: Gutted, Hashed and Deboned: Necroticism: Descanting the Insalubrious By Carcass At 35
quietus.description: Keith Kahn-Harris looks back at a landmark release full of surprises and possibilities To push back a genre label is, all too often, a reliably generic move by artists desperately seeking to differentiate themselves from other artists who sound much the same. Occasionally though, pushing back against genre label is a more subversive move, the mark of an artist pushing against anything that would close off their creative development. Such is the case with Carcass. It didn’t take them long at the start of their career to reject the grindcore label, they are currently rebelling against the extreme metal label, and on Necroticism: Descanting The Insalubrious they were reluctant to be labelled…

quietus.title: Music of the Month: The Best Albums and Tracks of October 2026
quietus.description: As we hurtle through the final months of 2026, tQ's staffers select another round-up of everything we've loved over the last few weeks We are only a few weeks away from end-of-year chartmageddon, the point at which we will be forced, whether we like it or not, to put on the record what defined our 2026. Given that a person's relationship with music is constantly-shifting – I find that the side of bed I've woken up on can determine whether a song makes me feel ecstatic or annoyed – I've always found the idea of making a permanent declaration of what's 'best' slightly daunting. I have a soft spot, by contrast, for the simplicity these more casual roundups, presented unranked and ad...

quietus.title: Andy Stott – Late Loop
quietus.description: Andy Stott Late Loop The British electronic music producer proves himself, once again, a consummate perfectionist – but it's the subtle imperfections that make his music really sing It didn’t take Andy Stott long to find himself drawn towards the frayed edges, to wear and imperfections. Less concerned with gleaming dancefloor patterns than the accumulation of hiss and grit, he made his name with slower tempos, tracks that went a little wonky, marked by age and rust. A sound in love with the ‘stuff’ of sound, the sense it had a physical surface that got under your fingernails, that carried the marks of time. On Late Loop it settles to a stillness, a richly emotive minimalism under the slow…

quietus.title: Audiovisual Phantasmagoria: Highlights from Semibreve 2026
quietus.description: Pedro João Santos reports from the latest edition of Portugal’s premiere festival for experimental music, where stellar sets from Noémi Büchi, Tygapaw, Marta Salogni and more lead the way Malcolm Pardon and Gustaf Broms, photo by Adriano Ferreira Borges / Semibreve A startled Jocy de Oliveira looks out at the sea: it’s well past time the grand piano should be brought ashore. She oversees a woman playing the ivories, drifting in the tide. “What do you expect to achieve this late?”, she blurts at the walkie-talkie, wrangling with the producers of her 2005 short film, Noturno De Um Piano. What starts off as an elegant allegory – the instrument set adrift in the ocean, a metaphor for the…

quietus.title: America’s Most Offensive? Ice Cube’s Death Certificate Revisited
quietus.description: Angus Batey looks back 35 years at the 360-degree attack of one of the most creatively independent yet offensive hip hop albums ever made. First published October 2011 Classic albums are supposed to be celebrated, but Death Certificate doesn't permit unqualified responses. It's a record made by a young man as talented at needling his listeners as he was at constructing and delivering some of the angriest lyrics in the hip hop canon, and is impossible to love without qualification. If you're not offended by a significant portion of it – no matter who you are, whatever your background – you're not listening properly. Just about the only universal reaction Death Certificate generates is one…

quietus.title: Put Your Hands In the Air: English Dancing Master by Leo Chadburn & Phaedra Ensemble
quietus.description: Leo Chadburn's latest work expands outwards from a seventeenth-century manual of folk dances to a kinetic exploration of human movement, from St Vitus' chorea to raving at Castlemorton Common English Dancing Master is a dance album, but not in the sense you would usually associate with the term. There is no “succession of repetitive beats” (the phrase used by the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 to criminalise outdoor raves), ribcage splintering bass or woozy toplines. Instead, we are treated to a reticent male narrator – voiced by Leo Chadburn – and the Phaedra Ensemble in conversation with each other. In fact, it’s not really an album at all but a singular radiophonic piece…

quietus.title: Maria W Horn – Melting Pillars of Snow
quietus.description: Maria W Horn Melting Pillars of Snow Melting Pillar of Snow is a dense exploration of time and decay that feels more like a static monument than a living listening experience Melting Pillars of Snow by Maria W Horn On Melting Pillars of Snow, Swedish composer Maria W Horn attempts to map the relentless passage of time across five expansive compositions. The record sets out to chart the friction between microscopic moments and deep historical time. Yet for all its conceptual weight and formal intent, the listening experience remains curiously remote, leaving the pieces sounding like static, glass-encased dioramas which may be meticulously assembled, but are emotionally lacking in power.…

quietus.title: Coming Up for Air: Andy Stott’s Favourite Albums
quietus.description: From 80s synth pop and 90s trip hop through to mischievous, glitched-out electronics, Andy Stott talks through 13 records that hold significance to him ahead of the release of his new album, Late Loop Across a career that now spans more than two decades, Andy Stott’s name has become synonymous with a style of electronic music that is patient and understated. Early records like Passed Me By and Luxury Problems dealt in dubbed-out minimalism and hauntingly gritty chuggers, while albums like 2016’s Too Many Voices and 2019’s It Should Be Us retained some of those qualities while introducing shades of dream pop into his captivating oeuvre. On new record Late Loop, which is his first studio LP…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Jason Dungan & Johan Carøe :: Routine
aquariumdrunkard.description: Copenhagen-based composers Jason Dungan (Blue Lake) and Johan Carøe join forces on Routine , a quietly transportive collection of ambient folk and new age soundscapes shaped through an exchange of musical fragments. Blending acoustic instrumentation, electronics, and Dungan’s self-designed 36-string zither, the duo arrive at something intimate and unhurried—a luminous meditation on domestic ritual, the rhythms of everyday life, and the quiet wonder of being alive.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Panamint :: S/T
aquariumdrunkard.description: Panamint began as a studio experiment between longtime collaborators Anna St. Louis and producer Jarvis Taveniere, who reunited to put Taveniere’s new Los Angeles studio through its paces. What started with left-field covers of Post Malone and Helene Smith soon evolved into a set of original recordings, joined by Danny Garcia, aka Reverend Baron. Out this week, their self-titled debut EP draws on the timeless pull of vintage soul and classic pop.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sam Gendel :: Advanced White Trash
aquariumdrunkard.description: In his classic book Mythologies, French thinker Roland Barthes criticizes plastic because it can be molded into anything—cheap, colorful surfaces open to infinite transformation. Contemporary pop is made of the same stuff, and Sam Gendel’s Advanced White Trash makes the case for what’s beautiful, even freeing, about it. The record sounds like something that was uploaded to SoundCloud at 3 a.m., a Roland Sound Canvas emulator buffering on a dying phone someone found in a Walmart parking lot, and still it comes out strangely appealing, almost hypnotic.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ana Palindrome :: A MAN A CURE
aquariumdrunkard.description: Cork trio Ana Palindrome make a hypnotic blend of art-pop, droning vocals, sawing fiddle, and glitchy folktronica on “A MAN A CURE,” their first release for London’s World of Echo. Beneath its pulsing rhythms and woozy electronics, the track questions the idea of self-made identity, as Niamh Dalton’s voice shifts between the organic and the artificial.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Show (The Halloween Edition)

aquariumdrunkard.title: Boards of Canada :: Hi Scores
aquariumdrunkard.description: Earlier this year, Boards of Canada unexpectedly released their fifth album Inferno , a case of an influential artist demonstrating that their style remains eminently relatable in 2026 a.d. To close out the year, the group has dipped into its archives, re-releasing the 1996 EP Hi Scores . There’s plenty to savor here, especially for longtime BOC listeners, but there’s also something compelling about being able to hear the group’s roots in such close temporal proximity to their current venture.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Shabazz Palaces
aquariumdrunkard.description: Our guest this week on the show, Ishmael Butler of Shabazz Palaces and Digable Planets, is used to swimming in waters where science fiction weirdness and musical expression mingle. Shabazz Palaces' new album, It’s a Style Sport , represents a new high water mark for the Seattle-based rapper; at once memoiristic and mystical, it’s a strange and beguiling listen. This week, he joins Transmissions host Jason P. Woodbury to discuss basketball, his "Afro-fractal" artistic approach, the influence of artists like the Cocteau Twins, and of course, that goofy old standby: what's it like being a middle aged guy in rap?

aquariumdrunkard.title: All Hallows’ Aquarium Drunkard III
aquariumdrunkard.description: The music of autumn comes in many shades, but none of them without a little smoke and shadow. The days are growing shorter, the air a little cooler, and it is once again time to light the jack-o-lanterns. In our third installment of All Hallows' Aquarium Drunkard , the writers reveal the secrets of their spooky season soundtracks. Inside you'll find doomed teenagers, dissociative episodes, ghost planets, grisly murders and all sorts of monsters, real and imagined. Whatever kind of menace you are looking for, we've got you covered.

mubi.description: One Sings, the Other Doesn't (Agnès Varda, 1977). In her memoir, Varda par Agnès , the French director describes herself as “une féministe de terrain plus qu’une discuteuse,” roughly translated as “a feminist on the ground rather than in theory.” Later in the book, she describes the “feminists” discussing her work, implying that she was outside this group. How feminist she reads from any angle now is unclear. Many would, for instance, find her focus on the body and childbirth essentialist. Her 1975 short, Réponse de femmes: Notre corps, notre sexe ( Women Reply: Our Bodies, Our Sex ), opens with this prompt: “What does it mean to be a woman?” The text is painted on glass and held up by two…

A few months earlier, the same film had world premiered at Cannes, in the Un Certain Regard section, and walked away with a special mention for the Caméra d’Or. It was the first Nigerian film to be programmed in the official selection at the festival. Variety called Akinola Davies Jr.’s film miraculous. Rotten Tomatoes aggregated the critical assessment as 98% positive. However, there exists a cultural invisibility at home that stands against these genuine international recognitions.
